\\\"circular\\\" problem in Spring can occur if:\\n- Two or more beans depend on each other (A needs B, B needs A), which causes Spring to have trouble wiring them.\\n- Your customizations or microservices, often including logging `RestTemplate` calls via interceptors.\\n\\nIf you use their logging features, **be careful not to inject RestTemplate into your logging classes (or their dependencies)**.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 3. **Example of Circular Problem**\\nSuppose:\\n\\n```java\\n@Bean\\npublic RestTemplate restTemplate(CustomLoggingInterceptor interceptor) { \\n    RestTemplate restTemplate = new RestTemplate();\\n    restTemplate.getInterceptors().add(interceptor);\\n    return restTemplate;\\n}\\n\\n@Component\\npublic class CustomLoggingInterceptor implements ClientHttpRequestInterceptor {\\n    // If you inject RestTemplate here, that's bad!\\n    public CustomLoggingInterceptor(SomeService service) { ... }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nIf `SomeService` also uses `RestTemplate`, you have a circular problem:\\n- `RestTemplate` needs the `interceptor`\\n- the `interceptor` needs `SomeService`\\n- `SomeService` needs `RestTemplate`\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 4. **How to Fix the Circular Dependency**\\n\\n### a) **Do NOT inject RestTemplate into its own interceptors/dependencies.**\\nYou can use `@Lazy` or refactor to break the circle. For example, don't inject `RestTemplate` into `CustomLoggingInterceptor`.\\n\\n### b) **Split Logging Logic and Service Logic.**\\nExtract logging logic so it doesn't need `RestTemplate`.\\n\\n### c) **Use Application Events.**\\nIf your logging system needs information from HTTP requests made by RestTemplate, publish application events from the interceptor and handle them elsewhere.\\n\\n### d) **Example: Correct Usage**\\n```java\\n@Bean\\npublic RestTemplate restTemplate(CustomLoggingInterceptor interceptor) { \\n    RestTemplate restTemplate = new RestTemplate();\\n    restTemplate.getInterceptors().add(interceptor);\\n    return restTemplate;\\n}\\n\\n@Component\\npublic class CustomLoggingInterceptor implements ClientHttpRequestInterceptor {\\n    // No RestTemplate injected here!\\n}\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 5. **Resources**\\n- [Spring Official on Circular **Example of Circular Problem**\\nSuppose:\\n\\n```java\\n@Bean\\npublic RestTemplate restTemplate(CustomLoggingInterceptor interceptor) { \\n    RestTemplate restTemplate = new RestTemplate();\\n `RestTemplate` needs the `interceptor`\\n- the `interceptor` needs `SomeService`\\n- `SomeService` needs `RestTemplate`\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 4. **How to Fix the Circular Dependency**\\n\\n### a) **Do NOT inject RestTemplate into its own interceptors/dependencies.**\\nYou can use `@Lazy` or refactor to break the circle. For example, don't inject `RestTemplate` into `CustomLoggingInterceptor`.\\n\\n### b) **Split Logging Logic and Service Logic.**\\nExtract logging logic so it doesn't need `RestTemplate`.\\n\\n### c) **Use Application Events.**\\nIf your logging system needs information from HTTP requests made by RestTemplate, publish application events from the interceptor and handle them elsewhere.\\n\\n### d) **Example: Correct Usage**\\n```java\\n@Bean\\npublic RestTemplate restTemplate(CustomLoggingInterceptor interceptor) { \\n    RestTemplate restTemplate = new RestTemplate();\\n in Spring can occur if:\\n- Two or more beans depend on each other (A needs B, B needs A), which causes Spring to have trouble wiring them.\\n- Your customizations or interceptors on `RestTemplate` might be referencing beans that also use `RestTemplate`.\\n- You're trying to log requests inside `RestTemplate` (e.g., with a custom interceptor) and that logger or service itself tries to use `RestTemplate`.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 2. **What does \\\"piomin/spring-boot-logging\\\" do?**\\nThe `piomin/spring-boot-logging` repo offers advanced logging for Spring Boot microservices, often including logging `RestTemplate` calls via interceptors.\\n\\nIf you use their logging features, **be careful not to inject RestTemplate into your logging classes (or their dependencies)**.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 3. **Example of Circular Problem**\\nSuppose:\\n\\n```java\\n@Bean\\npublic RestTemplate restTemplate(CustomLoggingInterceptor interceptor) { \\n    RestTemplate restTemplate = new RestTemplate();\\n    restTemplate.getInterceptors().add(interceptor);\\n    return restTemplate;\\n}\\n\\n@Component\\npublic class CustomLoggingInterceptor implements ClientHttpRequestInterceptor {\\n    // If you inject `RestTemplate` needs the `interceptor`\\n- the `interceptor` needs `SomeService`\\n- `SomeService` needs `RestTemplate`\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 4. **How to Fix the Circular Dependency**\\n\\n### a) **Do NOT inject RestTemplate into its own interceptors/dependencies.**\\nYou can use `@Lazy` or refactor to break the circle.
